assessment.summary: Twenty-one findings support three cross-cutting opportunities: proof-backed chain evidence, trusted operator provisioning, and bounded operation lifecycles.

nonNegotiables: Preserve Sompi's stable Purchase model independently of AP2 and x402 wire or SDK types.
Keep AP2 authorization and Kaspa-x402 payment execution at separate seams.
Do not create a universal payment-rail plugin system or require changes to the sibling Kaspa-x402 repository.
Keep the Trusted Authority deterministic, non-agentic, separately credentialed, and isolated from the MCP process.
Commit durable intent, reservation, idempotency, and recovery state before irreversible blockchain or Merchant effects.
Remain human-present, Kaspa-x402 exact, and Testnet-10 until recorded acceptance gates pass.
assumptions: No measured latency, memory, storage, throughput, or availability budget was supplied.
A balanced security and delivery profile is appropriate for the current clean cutover.
Hardening outputs are derived design artifacts and do not remediate findings.
The scan was in final reporting and unsealed when this analysis was produced.

opportunities.title: Proof-backed chain evidence and finality
opportunities.summary: Give Settlement, recovery, wallet, vault, and staging one owned proof-level and finality boundary.
opportunities.diagnosis: Thirteen findings arise because raw current-view RPC and Merchant-selected finality facts are interpreted independently by several privileged state machines.

evidence.claim: One selected RPC supplies UTXO membership and the DAA values used to create verified Settlement.
One selected RPC can fabricate recovery finality that releases policy capacity.
Generic RPC error text can become affirmative absence evidence.
Verbose RPC metadata can bypass canonical mempool transaction hashing.
Current UTXO and mempool views lose payment evidence after the Merchant output is spent.
One negative RPC snapshot can authorize a competing recovery broadcast.
Mempool exact-winner evidence can enter a terminal recovery state without the required-finality check.
A provisional wallet observation can durably complete a direct send.
Provisional outputs can advance the durable vault continuation.
A provisional deposit observation can commit durable vault state.
Provisional Purchase staging can commit vault and staging state.
Merchant-selected mempool finality can control recovery capacity release.
Current views lose staging-winner attribution after the winner output is spent.
Proof level, identity, history, and finality policy are owned by dispersed callers rather than one high-assurance boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every durable Settlement, capacity release, direct-Treasury completion, vault continuation, and staging commit consumes proof meeting a Sompi-owned operator minimum.
Mempool evidence is always provisional and cannot terminalize state or release capacity.
Transaction identity is derived from canonical bytes or verified proof, never untrusted verbose metadata alone.
A single negative RPC snapshot is unknown and cannot authorize a competing irreversible broadcast.
Accepted transaction and winner evidence survives output spend, restart, and the required recovery/accounting horizon.
Proof profile, verifier identity, canonical facts, finality, and digest are durable before proof-dependent state transitions.

options.title: Local observer guards
options.summary: Patch every current observer with typed errors, canonical transaction hashing, accepted-finality floors, recoverable provisional states, and history checks.

findingCoverage.rationale: Independent authenticity remains necessary after local tuple and finality hardening.
Coherent DAA and finality checks reduce the path, but one RPC still supplies all chain facts.
Typed capability and not-found handling prevents errors from becoming absence evidence.
Canonical local transaction hashing removes trust in verbose RPC identity.
Historical lookup and persistence help only to the extent the current backend retains trustworthy history.
Negative observations remain non-authorizing, but the current backend still lacks authenticated global absence.
The exact-winner branch enforces required finality and provisional outcomes remain recoverable.
Direct wallet completion requires the operator finality floor.
Vault continuation commits only after the operator finality floor.
Vault deposit commits only after the operator finality floor.
Purchase staging commits only after the operator finality floor.
Merchant finality cannot lower the operator minimum or bypass its trusted display.
Historical winner lookup reduces ambiguity but remains dependent on backend history.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closes known provisional, identity, and error-classification paths, but a selected RPC still controls positive chain facts and future callers can drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run all thirteen PoCs and search every durable consumer of RPC observations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Most guards are local; history checks add RPC calls only on affected recovery paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark current and guarded Settlement and recovery p50/p95/p99 latency under identical RPC fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Canonical hashing and typed outcomes use bounded temporary values; retained history adds durable storage rather than material heap.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS and retained history bytes across representative Purchases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provisional outcomes remain recoverable, though stricter finality and history requirements can leave more operations pending.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject mempool eviction, RPC disagreement, pruning, and restart and measure unresolved duration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dispersed guards need separate metrics and can produce different pending reasons.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review dashboards and incident traces for every observer before rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: Focused changes preserve current APIs, but journal transitions made under weak semantics cannot safely be reinterpreted.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run schema/restart tests and document rollback for each changed terminal state.

residualRisks: One malicious selected RPC can still self-attest positive chain facts.
History availability and authenticity remain backend-dependent.
Finality policy can drift in future call sites.

workPackages: Add typed RPC errors and canonical hashing.
Enforce operator finality floors and nonterminal provisional states.
Persist/query accepted transaction history.
Add targeted PoC regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: All thirteen original PoCs fail before a durable false or terminal effect.
Mempool evidence never completes or releases capacity.
Post-spend history can attribute accepted payment and recovery winners.
migrationNotes: Land as tactical protections before any structural cutover.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert only to a schema-compatible release; never reinterpret new terminal/history records using weaker semantics.

options.title: Typed Chain Evidence Gateway
options.summary: Centralize canonical identity, proof verification, history, negative evidence, source identity, and operator finality policy behind one Sompi-owned internal boundary.

findingCoverage.rationale: A selected RPC cannot mint accepted proof alone; absent proof or independent witness remains unknown.
Capacity release consumes a proof-level winner rather than an RPC-labelled finality.
Gateway results distinguish not-found, capability failure, timeout, disagreement, and unknown.
Gateway derives transaction identity canonically before issuing any proof-level result.
Accepted transaction proof is retained beyond current output lifetime.
One negative view cannot create a readiness capability for a conflicting broadcast.
Proof-level state types prevent mempool evidence from entering a terminal accepted state.
Direct wallet completion consumes an accepted proof at the operator floor.
Durable vault continuation consumes an accepted proof at the operator floor.
Durable vault deposit consumes an accepted proof at the operator floor.
Purchase staging consumes an accepted proof at the operator floor.
Operator finality policy is owned once and Merchant input may only strengthen it.
Historical winner proof preserves exact-versus-recovery attribution after spend.

tradeoffs.assessment: Branded proof-level results make unsafe promotion difficult and eliminate dispersed finality ownership; authenticity still depends on the admitted backend profile.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require every PoC to stop at Unknown unless a proof or accepted independent witness is present.

tradeoffs.assessment: Proof or witness collection adds network hops and makes latency depend on required sources; parallelism and bounded caching may contain it.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95/p99 proof latency, calls per proof, cache hit rate, and timeouts against the current observer.

tradeoffs.assessment: In-flight proof values and a bounded cache add modest memory; durable accepted history grows with transactions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS, cache bytes, and retained proof bytes per Purchase under a defined retention horizon.

tradeoffs.assessment: Disagreement and unavailable proof become coherent pending states instead of false terminal state, at the cost of deliberate fail-closed availability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault proof backends, witnesses, cache, restart, and history and measure unresolved duration and safe recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: The gateway needs proof-source identity, disagreement, downgrade, history-miss, and pending-age telemetry.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise incident runbooks with one source stale, unavailable, or disagreeing.

tradeoffs.assessment: All consumers and journal proof metadata change, though read-only shadow mode permits comparison before cutover.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run shadow comparison to an agreed mismatch threshold, then remove old direct terminal paths in one clean cutover.

residualRisks: Independent witnesses can collude or share an operational failure domain.
A proof profile can be specified incorrectly for Kaspa DAG finality or reorg behavior.
Fail-closed proof unavailability can reduce service availability.

workPackages: Define proof-level types and allowed profiles.
Implement a proof/witness backend and historical index contract.
Add journal proof metadata.
Cut exact, recovery, wallet, vault, and staging consumers over.
Remove replaced direct RPC terminal paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the gateway can mint proof-level values.
Every mapped state transition requires the correct proof level.
No single selected RPC can create accepted proof.
Original PoCs and crash/restart suites pass.
migrationNotes: Shadow the gateway read-only before journal cutover.
Do not keep permanent dual runtime paths.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before cutover, disable shadow calls; after cutover, roll back only to a release that understands the proof metadata and never silently downgrades profiles.

options.title: Trusted local evidence plane
options.summary: Back the typed gateway with an operator-controlled Kaspa node and retained accepted-transaction history on an authenticated local channel.

findingCoverage.rationale: A locally controlled consensus source supplies gateway proof instead of one selected remote RPC.
Local accepted-chain state and history authenticate the recovery winner before release.
Local evidence-plane APIs return typed absence and capability outcomes.
Canonical local transaction identity does not depend on remote verbose metadata.
The retained accepted-transaction index preserves paid-output history.
Local accepted history and gateway policy prevent one remote negative snapshot from authorizing recovery.
Proof-level state and local accepted evidence keep mempool outcomes provisional.
Direct wallet completion requires local accepted proof.
Vault continuation requires local accepted proof.
Vault deposit requires local accepted proof.
Purchase staging requires local accepted proof.
Operator finality policy and local accepted evidence prevent mempool capacity release.
The local history index preserves staging-winner attribution.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes ordinary dependence on one selected remote RPC for consensus and history, while making the local node/index a trusted component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run all PoCs with malicious public RPC telemetry and require local accepted proof for every terminal effect.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local steady-state queries may be faster, but synchronization, indexing, and gateway serialization add unmeasured costs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure sync/rebuild time and steady-state p50/p95/p99 query latency against remote and gateway baselines.

tradeoffs.assessment: A full node and history index require substantial process memory and persistent storage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS, disk growth, compaction, and retained bytes over a representative chain/history horizon.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local control improves evidence availability after sync, but the node/index becomes a shared dependency whose staleness or corruption must fail closed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject restart, lag, corruption, stale tip, index loss, and rebuild while measuring safe service behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Node lifecycle, version pinning, disk, synchronization, indexing, backup/rebuild, monitoring, and on-call ownership are new obligations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a timed rebuild and incident exercise with documented ownership and alert thresholds.

tradeoffs.assessment: The evidence plane is a new deployed component, but consumers remain stable if Option 2 lands first.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deploy behind the gateway, shadow results, prove health gates, then change only the permitted proof profile.

residualRisks: The local node, host, or history index can be compromised, stale, or corrupted.
Reorg and finality policy errors remain possible.
Node resource exhaustion can deny every proof-dependent workflow.

workPackages: Deploy and pin the local node.
Build retained accepted history and authenticated local access.
Integrate as a gateway proof profile.
Add backup, rebuild, monitoring, and failure procedures.
acceptanceCriteria: Public RPC lies cannot create terminal state.
Post-spend winner and payment evidence remains available for the required horizon.
Stale or unhealthy local evidence fails closed.
Rebuild and rollback procedures are demonstrated.
migrationNotes: Implement after the gateway so consumer APIs do not change again.
Keep mainnet disabled until the evidence plane and independent review pass.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Permit rollback only to another explicitly configured gateway proof profile; never fall back silently to a selected remote RPC.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the typed gateway for the current testnet cutover, retain local guards during migration, and require the trusted local evidence plane or equivalent verified proof before public/mainnet claims.

opportunities.title: Trusted operator provisioning and configuration provenance
opportunities.summary: Represent vault ownership, Treasury policy, and supported Merchant transport as one authenticated operator control-plane object.
opportunities.diagnosis: Four findings arise because documented operator intent enters through Agent arguments, permissive flags, or filesystem bytes without one enforced provenance and semantic-validation boundary.

evidence.claim: Agent-facing vault_create accepts the owner recovery key and cap.
The supported runtime parser can explicitly permit unauthenticated HTTP Merchant transport.
Vault creation checks key length/hex but does not parse a valid x-only curve point.
Policy hot reload follows a path and mtime without enforcing file provenance before wallet authorization.
Strong local provenance primitives already exist but do not own all operator configuration.

desiredInvariants: Vault recovery authority and consensus cap are installed through a trusted operator ceremony, never Agent-facing MCP input.
Every recovery public key is parsed as a valid pinned x-only curve point before persistence or covenant construction.
The supported Treasury-capable profile permits authenticated HTTPS Merchant transport only.
Operator configuration is read through stable owner/mode/link/inode checks and activated as a canonical versioned digest.
Policy reservations, vault configuration, and relevant operations record the exact active configuration revision.
Agent tools can request and inspect work but cannot create or loosen operator configuration.

options.title: Local provenance guards
options.summary: Harden each existing path with operator-only key input, pinned curve parsing, secure descriptor-based policy reads, and HTTPS-only transport.

findingCoverage.rationale: Owner recovery key and cap are removed from Agent input and read from an operator-controlled secure source.
The supported Treasury runtime rejects HTTP.
The pinned SDK parser validates every owner point before persistence.
Policy reads enforce regular-file, owner, mode, no-follow, parent, and stable-inode provenance.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closes the observed paths but leaves operator identity, schema, activation, and audit duplicated across subsystems.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run all four PoCs and review every operator-owned configuration consumer.

tradeoffs.assessment: Curve parsing and filesystem metadata checks occur at setup/startup or reload, not on the network critical path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure startup and reload latency before and after the checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded parsed key, policy, and stat values are retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare process RSS across startup and repeated safe reloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unsafe deployments fail closed, though previously tolerated symlinks or modes can prevent startup/reload.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test all file replacement and restart cases and measure failure/recovery duration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Several secure-file ceremonies, digests, and error paths remain for operators to understand.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the setup and recovery runbooks on a clean host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Focused changes preserve most runtime APIs, but Agent vault setup and HTTP deployments must change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory current configuration and exercise one clean import without fallback paths.

residualRisks: Future operator configuration paths can omit equivalent provenance checks.
An intentionally approved unsafe policy remains effective.
Operator identity and activation audit remain dispersed.

workPackages: Remove owner key/cap from MCP input.
Parse x-only points through the pinned SDK.
Secure policy descriptor/path reads.
Reject HTTP in the supported runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: All four PoCs fail before authority or signing sinks.
No unsafe file provenance is accepted.
Valid operator setup and HTTPS Purchases still pass.
migrationNotes: Use as immediate protection before a manifest cutover.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert code only with a compatible operator configuration; do not restore Agent recovery input or HTTP as an operational workaround.

options.title: Operator-provisioned manifest
options.summary: Validate and atomically install one versioned manifest under secure local state, then give runtime components immutable typed projections and record its digest.

findingCoverage.rationale: An operator-only installer supplies recovery authority; MCP can only report readiness.
The manifest schema makes HTTP incompatible with the supported Treasury profile.
Manifest validation parses and validates the exact x-only point before activation.
Secure installation, stable read, typed projection, revision, and digest replace raw policy-file hot reload.

tradeoffs.assessment: One owned boundary enforces principal, provenance, semantic cross-field checks, and activation identity across the four controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run all PoCs plus malformed/cross-field manifest tests and verify no consumer parses raw configuration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Canonical parse, validation, and hashing occur at startup or deliberate activation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure setup, startup, and reload latency against the current configuration path.

tradeoffs.assessment: One immutable parsed manifest replaces several small parsed objects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare steady-state RSS and retained configuration objects.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic activation and one revision improve coherence; malformed replacement can deliberately block activation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault partial writes, fsync, inode replacement, restart, and rollback while checking last-verified behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: One preview/validate/install command, digest, revision, and runbook replace multiple conventions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Conduct a clean-host provisioning and rollback exercise and collect operator errors.

tradeoffs.assessment: Vault, policy, egress, runtime config, and journal audit bindings change together.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Preview-import existing values, require operator review, then perform a no-fallback clean cutover.

residualRisks: A central parser or installer defect affects several controls.
Operator compromise or intentionally unsafe policy remains authoritative.
Hot reload, if retained, can introduce rollback or activation complexity.

workPackages: Specify canonical manifest and version.
Build preview/validate/install ceremony.
Project typed vault, policy, and HTTPS configuration.
Bind revision/digest to durable records.
Delete replaced Agent/file/HTTP paths.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP cannot select recovery authority.
Unsafe keys, files, profiles, and HTTP combinations fail before activation.
Activation is atomic and auditable.
Original PoCs and restart tests pass.
migrationNotes: Import current values only into a reviewable preview.
Remove old runtime paths in the same cutover.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore a previously verified manifest revision understood by the same runtime; never fall back to Agent arguments, raw policy paths, or HTTP.

options.title: Signed offline bundle
options.summary: Wrap the canonical manifest in a dedicated operator signature and verify trust root, semantics, and monotonic revision at runtime.

findingCoverage.rationale: A signed operator bundle, not MCP input, selects recovery authority.
Signed semantics still reject HTTP in the supported Treasury profile.
Bundle semantic validation rejects invalid x-only points.
Signature and monotonic revision authenticate bytes delivered through an untrusted path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authenticates configuration across untrusted distribution and rejects rollback, but creates a high-value signing key and trust root.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run all PoCs plus forgery, trust-root, rollback, and signer-rotation tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: One signature verification occurs at activation rather than on the payment path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure verification and activation latency for representative bundle sizes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Verification retains only bounded bundle, signature, and trust metadata.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare activation peak RSS against Option 2.

tradeoffs.assessment: Untrusted distribution becomes tolerable, but lost signing keys or monotonic revision state can block updates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise lost signer, damaged revision state, rotation, recovery, and signed rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Key generation, offline custody, backup, rotation, revocation, signing, distribution, and audit are new obligations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete an end-to-end ceremony and timed recovery with named ownership.

tradeoffs.assessment: Builds cleanly on the manifest but adds trust-root and signature-envelope migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Adopt only after Option 2 semantics are stable, then migrate one test instance through key rotation.

residualRisks: Signing-key compromise can authorize every receiving instance.
A valid signature does not make unsafe semantics safe.
Trust-root and monotonic-revision recovery can deny configuration updates.

workPackages: Define signature envelope and algorithm.
Provision separate signing trust root.
Implement verification and revision checks.
Document rotation, revocation, backup, and signed rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: Forged, old, wrong-network, wrong-signer, and semantically unsafe bundles fail closed.
Rotation and recovery are demonstrated.
Original PoCs remain blocked.
migrationNotes: Adopt only when configuration crosses a real host or administrative boundary.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Rollback requires a deliberately signed higher-revision bundle; never replay an older revision.

opportunities.recommendation: Use one secure local operator manifest for the current single-host product; add signatures only when real multi-host or offline distribution justifies the new credential lifecycle.

opportunities.title: Bounded, cancellable operation lifecycles
opportunities.summary: Require admission, aggregate budget, cancellation or absolute expiry, terminal outcome, and exactly-once release for every retained resource.
opportunities.diagnosis: Four findings retain sockets, prompt work, immutable evidence bytes, policy capacity, or the direct-Treasury slot beyond the event that should release them.

evidence.claim: Incomplete unauthenticated sockets consume an unbounded set under a resettable inactivity timeout.
Authenticated decisions enter an unbounded uncancellable terminal prompt tail.
Unique request bodies become immutable evidence before reversible egress validation and without aggregate quota.
A durable intent claim precedes SDK preparation, but permanent pre-submission failure has no terminal release transition.
Durability is correctly required before irreversible effects, but retained resources lack one complete admission-to-release contract.

desiredInvariants: Every scarce resource acquired for untrusted work has an aggregate budget, owner, absolute lifetime, terminal outcome, and idempotent release path.
Pre-authentication Authority work uses a short non-renewable deadline; the human-decision timeout starts only after authenticated admission.
One AbortSignal follows an Authority decision across transport, service, prompt queue, and terminal input.
Reversible validation and transactional capacity admission occur before immutable Purchase/evidence creation.
Proven permanent pre-submission Treasury failures terminalize and release atomically; transient or ambiguous failures remain bound to the original identity.
Authority admission remains inside the Authority process, while Purchase/evidence and Treasury admission remain in the Purchase Journal.

options.title: Local limits and terminalization
options.summary: Add focused caps, absolute deadlines, cancellation, aggregate evidence quota, prevalidation ordering, and a safe Treasury terminal failure path.

findingCoverage.rationale: A fixed pre-authentication permit count and absolute frame deadline bound retained sockets.
A bounded prompt queue and propagated cancellation remove disconnected, expired, lease-lost, and shutdown work.
Egress validation precedes durability and a transactional aggregate quota bounds accepted evidence.
SDK prevalidation and a restricted intent-to-failed-terminal transition release proven pre-submission failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closes the four reproduced retention paths, though future resources can omit equivalent aggregate/release controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run all four PoCs and audit every retained untrusted-work resource.

tradeoffs.assessment: Counters and cancellation are constant-time; transactional evidence quota adds a short database critical section before fsync.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark mixed hostile/legitimate authority and evidence workloads for p95/p99 latency and SQLite lock time.

tradeoffs.assessment: Socket and prompt memory becomes bounded; quota metadata adds small durable state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure descriptors, heap, RSS, timers, and queued items at and above configured caps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dead work releases resources, while low limits can reject legitimate bursts and misclassified Treasury errors can release unsafely.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject every cancellation, write, restart, and preparation failure and verify exactly-once release.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators gain several separate limits, overload errors, gauges, and repair paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise runbooks at each limit and verify alerts identify the owning subsystem.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authority changes are in memory; evidence quota and Treasury terminal state require compatible journal migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old/new restart and rollback tests with quota reservations and terminal rows.

residualRisks: Continuously admitted hostile work can still consume all available permits without a fairness identity.
Accepted legitimate evidence can still fill storage if retention is undefined.
Incorrect permanent-error classification can release Treasury capacity unsafely.

workPackages: Cap pre-auth and authenticated authority work.
Propagate cancellation through the prompt.
Move reversible Purchase admission before durability and add transactional quota.
Prevalidate Treasury input and add safe terminal preparation failure.
acceptanceCriteria: All four PoCs are bounded or rejected.
Every release path is exactly once.
No cancelled Authority work signs.
No ambiguous post-preparation Treasury state is terminalized.
migrationNotes: Use as direct containment before adopting a shared lifecycle contract.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Authority changes roll back by restart; durable rollback requires a schema-compatible version preserving quota and terminal history.

options.title: Per-boundary admission leases
options.summary: Give Authority, Purchase/evidence, and direct Treasury the same admission-to-release invariants while keeping enforcement and storage separate across trust boundaries.

findingCoverage.rationale: An Authority-owned pre-auth lease reserves and releases each socket under a fixed aggregate budget.
An authenticated decision lease carries cancellation and ownership through the bounded prompt scheduler.
A transactional Purchase/evidence capacity lease reserves unique bytes/count before fsync and releases on rejection or write failure.
The durable Treasury lease distinguishes permanent pre-effect failure from transient and ambiguous states and releases atomically.

tradeoffs.assessment: Makes owner, budget, cancellation, terminal outcome, and release explicit at each handoff without creating a cross-process broker.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Assert every admission/release edge and re-run all four PoCs plus retained-resource inventory review.

tradeoffs.assessment: Constant-time lease bookkeeping is small; durable evidence admission can serialize briefly on a quota row.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95/p99 admission latency, SQLite lock duration, fsync throughput, and event-loop delay.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authority sockets, handlers, and prompts have auditable bounded counts; durable lease metadata is small.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure counters, descriptors, timers, heap, RSS, and oldest item under sustained hostile load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deterministic reclamation and integrity checks improve recovery, while leaked or double-released leases can deny work or oversubscribe capacity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault every state transition and verify counters never leak, go negative, or exceed capacity across restart.

tradeoffs.assessment: Common lifecycle names make dashboards and incident reasoning coherent, though limits remain separately configured per process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run an overload incident exercise using admitted, active, expired, cancelled, released, and oldest-age metrics.

tradeoffs.assessment: Handoffs and durable schema change, but each trust boundary can cut over independently.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Roll out Authority, Purchase/evidence, and Treasury separately and delete superseded counters after each owner is active.

residualRisks: A shared vocabulary can become an overgeneralized runtime abstraction if resource-specific semantics are hidden.
A hostile client can monopolize permits without authenticated fairness.
Lease implementation bugs can leak or double-release resources.

workPackages: Define the lifecycle vocabulary and review checklist.
Implement Authority-local admission/cancellation.
Implement transactional Purchase/evidence capacity.
Complete direct-Treasury terminal outcome semantics.
Add common fault-injection assertions without a shared runtime broker.
acceptanceCriteria: Every retained object has one owner and active lease.
Aggregate usage never exceeds configured capacity.
Every terminal path releases exactly once.
Trust-boundary isolation remains intact.
Original PoCs and crash/restart suites pass.
migrationNotes: Remove duplicate counters and exception-only release behavior after ownership is established.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Authority in-memory rollback occurs by restart; durable rollback must preserve quota reservations and terminal Treasury history.

opportunities.recommendation: Use per-boundary admission leases with separate Authority and Purchase/Treasury enforcement; do not introduce a shared scheduler or weaken durable-before-effect ordering.

openQuestions: Which Kaspa proof or independently operated witness profile is acceptable for the current Testnet-10 Chain Evidence Gateway?
What accepted or confirmed finality floor applies to each Settlement, direct Treasury, vault, staging, and recovery transition?
What history retention horizon is required for policy accounting, recovery, and dispute evidence?
Should the operator manifest require process restart or support monotonic hot reload?
Which OS identity owns operator-manifest installation and which UID/GID must runtime verification require?
What are the initial socket, prompt, Purchase-count, evidence-byte, and decision-lifetime budgets?
Which Treasury preparation errors can be proven permanent before signing or submission?
What evidence or operational threshold will trigger adoption of the trusted local evidence plane or signed offline configuration bundle?
